sampling_model.compressed_gaussian_prediction: The dimensions, coefficient vector and covariance are fixed. The original observations follow def:observation-model and def:data-vectors; feature rows are independent Gaussian vectors with mean zero and covariance Sigma, and errors are independent Gaussian variables with variance sigma squared, independent of features. The full-row-rank sketch is independent of the data and may itself be random. The test pair is an independent observation from the same law. The coefficient vector is measurable with respect to def:compressed-information. Conditional distributions condition on that information, leaving the complementary observations random. This setting is used by thm:cpal-complementary-law.
sampling_model.balanced_gaussian_design: The dimensions, coefficient vector, covariance and constants are fixed. The whitened design has independent standard Gaussian entries and is independent of the sketch and structural error vector. Errors are iid, centered, uniformly sub-Gaussian with variance sigma squared, independent of the sketch and features. The sketch is independent of the data and has full row rank; it may be random. The test pair is independent from the same model. Constructions are def:sketched-least-squares, def:corrected-risk-estimates, and the notation conventions def:normalization-convention and def:derivative-convention. This setting is used by thm:cpal-corrected-accuracy, lem:dot-beta, lem:dot-r, lem:dot-rh, lem:dot-hxh, lem:dot-rxr, lem:dot-rxxr, lem:dot-hxxh, lem:opnorm-x-bound, lem:m-inverse-bound, lem:balanced-stein-sufficient-conditions, lem:balanced-moment-bounds, prop:stein-risk-from-moments, prop:q-identity-sigma, lem:balanced-remainder-bounds, lem:balanced-trace-stein-bounds, lem:balanced-exceptional-weight, and prop:trace-calibration-general. Conditional bounds integrate the design and errors holding the independent sketch fixed. The Appendix balanced-sketch results use the trace-normalized representative with $\trace(\bA)=n$, fixed positive spectral bounds and the eventual gap $m-d\geq\kappa n$ of Assumption~\ref{assu:Gaussian-Stein-design}. Design derivatives hold the sketch, population covariance, coefficient vector and structural errors fixed. This setting also supplies only the balanced-sketch specialization of lem:influence-from-moments; its direct mixed-moment inequalities retain their general law. In thm:cpal-corrected-accuracy normalization is a proof representative, not an extra condition on the original sketch scale, and the risk estimates remain invariant under that rescaling.
sampling_model.natural_scale_gaussian_sketch_comparison: The observations and independent test pair have the Gaussian law of compressed_gaussian_prediction, with positive noise variance. Dimensions, covariance and coefficients are fixed at each n. Scaled orthogonal sketches are independent of the data, with their scale allowed by the paper; dense Gaussian sketches instead have iid N(0,1/m) entries independently of the data. Fits and risk estimates are the nodes def:sketched-least-squares, def:corrected-risk-estimates and def:gcv-estimate, retaining their natural sketch scales. This setting is used by thm:cpal-risk-benchmarks. The scaled orthogonal specialization is used by thm:tight-frame-mse-comparison and thm:cpal-mse-comparison; MSE expectations average over training data and sketch randomness.
sampling_model.generic_derivative_fields: The dimensions are fixed and the matrices K,L and vectors q,r are random fields with respect to the design coordinates; no additional distributional law is imposed in lem:derivative-energy-from-inverse-moments. In lem:influence-from-moments the vectors are those of def:whitened-coordinates and expectations are with respect to the law under consideration; its direct inequalities use the corresponding mixed moments.
sampling_model.conditional_gaussian_fields: The dimensions are fixed. In lem:stein-remainders-from-moments, Z has iid standard Gaussian entries independent of (S,epsilon), and conditional calculations hold these latter objects fixed; q is a general field with the stated conditional smoothness. In lem:normalized-gaussian-stein, the sigma-field F is independent of an iid standard Gaussian Z, and the two general fields may depend on F and Z. Conditional expectations integrate Z holding F fixed. These general fields use def:derivative-energy, def:stein-fluctuations, def:normalized-energies, def:gaussian-contractions and def:conditional-energy. The same independent-$\mathcal F$ Gaussian design setting also applies to lem:matrix-gaussian-divergence-cited and lem:one-vector-second-order-cited: conditional on $\mathcal F$, their smooth fields depend on $\bZ$, derivatives hold $\mathcal F$ fixed, and conditional expectations integrate the Gaussian matrix.
sampling_model.auxiliary_response: The joint law of (X,S) remains its original balanced Gaussian-design marginal. The auxiliary response is given by def:auxiliary-response-law; its noise is a standard Gaussian vector independent of (X,S), and its coefficient vector is zero. Response quantities are the constructions identified in that definition. This law is used by lem:balanced-trace-stein-bounds and prop:trace-calibration-general, while the original response law is also used in lem:balanced-trace-stein-bounds.
sampling_model.rowwise_gaussian_covariance: The cited input lem:rowwise-gaussian-covariance-cited uses the setting of lem:stein-remainders-from-moments and its Gaussian-design, conditional smoothness and second-order moment premises. The positive dimensions $n,d$ are fixed. For distinct locally bound row indices $i,k$, condition on $(\bZ_{-\{i,k\}},\bS,\bep)$; the remaining two design rows are independent standard Gaussian vectors in $\R^d$. The conditional means, centered quadratic forms, cross-row Jacobians and weights are exactly def:rowwise-conditional-quantities and def:rowwise-jacobian-weights. Conditional calculations hold the remaining rows, sketch and errors fixed; the displayed expectation and weights then integrate the original law. The local row index $k$ has no connection to the finite-MSE abbreviation $k=m-d$. Bellec (2023), Lemma 7.1 is applied conditionally in this setting; no new assumption on the structural-error distribution is imposed.
